slides.texte_overlay:
Things that make you surprisingly
easy to talk to
Nod and react while people talk. A small "no way" or "wait, really?" shows you're right there with them. Talking to a blank face is exhausting. Talking to someone who reacts is easy.
Remember what people care about. Their dog, their exam, their brother's wedding. Ask about it next time. Nothing makes someone feel more at ease than realising you actually listened.
Have stories and questions ready. Five minutes a day of history, art or science and you're never short of something interesting. People love talking to someone who's curious.
slides.texte_sophia: I started doing five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now I'm never short of something interesting, and people love talking to me.

slides.texte_overlay: Don't correct small things. The wrong year, the wrong name of a band. Let it go unless it matters. Nobody enjoys talking to the guy who interrupts to fix every little detail.
Match their energy. Excited story, be excited. Quiet moment, slow down. People feel understood when you meet them where they are, and that's when conversations get easy.
Be fine with a little silence. Not every pause needs filling. Sip your drink, smile, look around. Calm silence feels comfortable. Nervous chatter is what makes people want to leave.
End with something warm. "Really good talking to you, let's do this again." People remember how a conversation ended, and a warm goodbye makes them want to talk to you again.
